timeline.title: The virtuous cycle of PLA
timeline.subtitle: How local corn becomes your favorite fidgets

step1.title: Culture & Harvest
step1.description: Non-food corn is grown locally, GMO-free, capturing CO₂ during its natural growth.

step2.title: Starch & Dextrose
step2.description: Harvested grains are ground to extract starch, which is then converted into dextrose (simple sugar).

step3.title: Polymerization
step3.description: Dextrose ferments into lactic acid, then is polymerized to create biodegradable PLA plastic pellets.

step4.title: Filament Extrusion
step4.description: Pellets are heated and stretched to produce a calibrated 1.75 mm diameter filament wound on a spool.

step5.title: 3D Printing
step5.description: The filament is melted at 215°C and deposited layer by layer by our printers in Comines to form your objects.

material.title: Raw Material // Bio-sourced PLA 🌱
material.p1: At Spoolio, we print fun, not pollution. Our objects don't come from a petrochemical factory on the other side of the world: they come to life in Comines, layer by layer, from bio-sourced PLA.
material.p2: It is a plant-based plastic made from cornstarch. Zero petroleum, zero overstock, zero nonsense. Just local, eco-friendly tech.
material.note_text: Like any good corn, it loves indoor comfort but hates being left in full sun on a 60°C car dashboard.
